meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in class. Who decided that?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now the essay.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing that down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he drafted somewhere else and pasted it in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, he'll bring it. Whatever happens next, none of this goes on his record and none of it happens in front of his class. Is there anything on his file right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A misquoted line is a mark off for sloppy research, not proof of anything. And you skipped my question, Hale: is anything on his file right now?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. Then tell me exactly what you're proposing, and I'll want it in writing that his file stays clean.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Two weeks later he changed his mind about Hamlet; that's called learning. Your proposal, Hale.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, so I'll take it, to put this behind him and nothing more. Tonight, in writing, with the date of the rewrite in it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. Who else in this building knows about the zero?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today that, under procedure 4.4, Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still want to know who else at the school knows about the zero, and I want every part of this agreement confirmed in writing. I expect that written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth under 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record; she still wants that confirmed in writing tonight and wants to know who else in the school knows, and this is the fair outcome, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her claim that he drafted elsewhere by asking for that draft with its date, and that held because she could check it and had no answer.
What cost ground: You twice went straight to new evidence without answering her direct question about whether anything was on his file, which made her sharper and kept her most important fear open longer than it needed to be.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on his file, answer it plainly in one sentence before showing the misquoted line, so her biggest fear is settled and your evidence lands on a calmer listener.
